newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy phone tariff cut plan should help cut CPI.
newsitem.headline: Italy phone tariff cut plan should help cut CPI.

text.p: Italian phone tariff cuts, which are under study and could come into effect from March 1, should help reduce consumer price inflation (CPI), Michele Lauria, under secretary at the Post Ministry said on Friday.
Lauria said in a statement issued by the ministry that the planned tariff cuts would benefit consumers "contributing, in addition, to an effective reduction of the general consumer price index."
The statement said the tariff reductions would help prepare state telecoms group Stet and its operating arm Telecom Italia for the liberalisation of the teleoms sector.
The statement said the tariff structure reform should coincide with the increase in phone rental charges, due to run from March 1.

The proposed cuts involve a strong reduction in trunk calls to be carried out in phases between March 1 and December 1997 and a reduction in international calls to major centres. This would be carried out in two phases starting in March.
A cut in line rental charges was also under consideration, to come into effect in December 1997 or January 1998.
Internet users will also be given favourable treatment.
Call from public call boxes would be unchanged. Milan newsroom +392-66102321
